species.title: Scots Pine
species.native_region: Eurasia

species.title: European Ash
species.native_region: Europe

species.title: Teak
species.native_region: South and Southeast Asia
species.description: Tropical hardwood with exceptional natural durability, dimensional stability, and resistance to rot, insects, and weather. Gold standard for shipbuilding and outdoor furniture.

species.title: Silver Birch
species.native_region: Eurasia
species.description: Pioneer tree producing bark for containers and canoes, timber for plywood, birch tar adhesive (one of oldest known adhesives), and edible sap.

species.title: English Oak
species.native_region: Europe
species.description: Foundational timber of Western civilization. Shipbuilding, barrel-making, structural beams, and tannin bark for leather production. Exceptionally durable heartwood.

species.title: Abaca
species.native_region: Philippines, Borneo
species.description: Tropical banana relative producing one of the strongest natural fibers. Saltwater-resistant rope, specialty paper, and cordage. Tensile strength 450-850 MPa.

species.title: New Zealand Flax
species.native_region: New Zealand
species.description: Perennial monocot producing strong leaf fiber for cordage, weaving, and thatching. Tensile strength 300-500 MPa. Extremely tough and adaptable. Tolerates salt, wet, and frost.

species.title: Sunn Hemp
species.native_region: India, Pakistan
species.description: Fast-growing tropical legume producing bast fiber for cordage and paper while fixing 60-120 kg nitrogen per hectare. Dual-value crop: fiber AND soil improvement.

species.title: Paper Mulberry
species.native_region: East Asia
species.description: Fast-growing tree cultivated for inner bark fiber used in tapa cloth and high-quality handmade paper. Long fiber (5-12 mm) bonds naturally when beaten.

species.title: True Indigo
species.native_region: Tropical Asia
species.description: Tropical legume producing the most important blue dye in human history. Contains indican which yields indigotin through fermentation and oxidation. Vat dye process.

species.title: Madder
species.native_region: Mediterranean, Western Asia
species.description: Perennial climbing plant producing alizarin, the most important red dye in history. Roots contain 1-4% dye compounds. Requires 2-3 years growth. Alum mordant produces Turkey red.

species.title: Woad
species.native_region: Southeastern Europe, Western Asia
species.description: Biennial herb producing the same indigotin as tropical indigo but from a temperate-climate plant. Only blue dye source available in temperate Europe for 2000+ years.

species.title: Guayule
species.native_region: Southwestern US, Northern Mexico
species.description: Desert shrub producing natural rubber (cis-1,4-polyisoprene) from stems. Only practical rubber source for arid climates. 5-20% rubber content in dry stems. Harvested whole-plant, not tapped.

species.title: India Rubber Tree
species.native_region: Northeast India, Myanmar
species.description: Large evergreen fig tree producing latex containing rubber. Lower yield than Hevea but tolerates cooler temperatures and poorer soils. Backup rubber source for subtropical regions.

species.title: Black Wattle
species.native_region: Southeastern Australia
species.description: Fast-growing tree producing bark with 30-40% tannin content, highest of any cultivated species. Primary global source of vegetable tannins for leather. 7-10 year rotation. Nitrogen-fixing.

species.title: Quebracho
species.native_region: Gran Chaco, South America
species.description: South American hardwood with 20-30% tannin in heartwood. Axe-breaker hardness (1200-1300 kg/m3 density). Produces firm, water-resistant leather with distinctive red-brown color.

species.title: Sicilian Sumac
species.native_region: Mediterranean, Western Asia
species.description: Mediterranean shrub with triple use: tannin-rich leaves (15-25%) for light leather, brown/black dye, and tart berries as spice. Gallotannin leather is soft, flexible, pale yellow.

species.title: White Willow
species.native_region: Europe, Western Asia
species.description: Deciduous tree whose bark contains salicin (0.5-1.5%), the aspirin precursor. Pain relief, fever reduction, anti-inflammatory. Also provides basketry withies from coppiced shoots.

species.title: Cinchona
species.native_region: Andes Mountains, South America
species.description: Andean tree producing quinine alkaloids (1-8% in bark), the most important antimalarial drug for 400 years. Requires montane tropical conditions. 6-8 years to first bark harvest.

species.title: Foxglove
species.native_region: Europe
species.description: Biennial herb producing cardiac glycosides (digoxin, digitoxin) for heart failure and atrial fibrillation treatment. Extremely poisonous. Therapeutic dose is 60-80% of toxic dose.

species.title: Ephedra
species.native_region: China, Mongolia
species.description: Arid-zone gymnosperm shrub producing ephedrine and pseudoephedrine (0.5-2.5% in stems). Bronchodilator for asthma, decongestant for colds. Grows in semi-desert conditions.

species.title: Sweet Wormwood
species.native_region: Temperate Asia
species.description: Annual herb producing artemisinin (0.1-1.0% in leaves), the most effective antimalarial known. Faster-acting than quinine. Also produces insect-repellent essential oil.

species.title: Tung Tree
species.native_region: Southern China
species.description: Subtropical tree producing seeds with 30-40% tung oil. Premier natural wood finish: dries harder and more water-resistant than linseed oil, does not darken with age.

species.title: Black Alder
species.native_region: Europe
species.description: Nitrogen-fixing tree producing timber highly resistant to decay when permanently submerged. Venice built on alder pilings. Also provides tannin bark and soil improvement.

species.title: Gum Arabic
species.native_region: Sahel, Africa
species.description: Sahelian tree exuding gum arabic: edible, water-soluble adhesive, emulsifier, and binder for ink, paint, food, and medicine. Traded across Sahara for 4000+ years.

species.title: Neem
species.native_region: Indian Subcontinent

species.title: Pyrethrum
species.native_region: Dalmatia, Croatia
species.description: Perennial daisy producing pyrethrins (0.5-2.0% in flowers), fast-acting contact insecticide. Extremely low mammalian toxicity. Degrades rapidly in sunlight, leaving no residue.

species.title: Moso Bamboo
species.native_region: China, Taiwan
species.description: Largest temperate bamboo. Tensile strength higher than steel by weight (350-500 MPa). Harvestable in 3-5 years. Culms 10-20m tall. Construction, scaffolding, paper, edible shoots.

species.title: Field Elm
species.native_region: Europe
species.description: European tree producing timber with interlocked grain that resists splitting. Traditional choice for wagon wheel hubs and water pipes. Withstands alternating wet and dry cycles.
